obligation: SEC Regulation S-K Item 106 (risk management, strategy and governance)
basis: SEC registrant and large accelerated filer that files Form 10-K; Item 1C has appeared since FY2023. No size relief applies to Item 106

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incidents)
basis: SEC registrant; not a smaller reporting company. Filing is due within four business days after the materiality determination

obligation: SOX section 404 and Exchange Act Rule 13a-15
basis: Large accelerated filer, so the auditor attestation in 7262(b) applies; Rule 13a-15(a)-(d) sets the quarterly disclosure controls evaluation and the annual ICFR evaluation

obligation: Federal Reserve computer-security incident notification (Regulation Y Subpart N)
basis: Applies to bank holding companies, savings and loan holding companies and the other entities in 225.300(c). No subsidiary is a bank or savings association, and Finance takes no deposits
analyzed_in: P08 (matrix row marked not applicable); P03

obligation: Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards
basis: Same reason as N55-R04: the group is not under Federal Reserve supervision. Finance is covered by the FTC Safeguards Rule instead

obligation: HIPAA (sponsored group health plan)
citation: 45 CFR 164.504(f); 45 CFR 164.314(b); 45 CFR Part 164, Subpart E
basis: The self-insured plan (about 21,000 covered lives) is a covered entity. The holding company, as plan sponsor, receives PHI for appeals and stop-loss, which is more than summary and enrollment information, so 164.504(f) and 164.314(b) apply. The plan's own Security Rule program is run by the benefits program and is outside these deliverables

obligation: CIRCIA (proposed)
basis: Proposed only; no final rule published at intake. Reporting to CISA is voluntary until a final rule takes effect. Recheck when final

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule
applies: Yes, for Finance; reaches the holding company as service provider
basis: Finance is a financial institution (314.1(b); 314.2(h)) with customer information on about 520,000 consumers, so the 314.6 exception does not apply. GBS runs Finance's identity, email, files, payroll, ACH, bank connectivity and security operations, so it is Finance's service provider (314.2(r); 314.4(f)). Finance employs its own Qualified Individual, so 314.4(a)(1)-(3) does not apply

obligation: Breach notification and data security laws of each state of residence
citation: Statutes of Florida, Georgia, Alabama, South Carolina, North Carolina, Tennessee and each state where affected individuals reside
basis: Employees, borrowers and customers live in the six operating states and elsewhere; notify under the law of each state where affected individuals reside

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (worked example)
basis: Each group company holds personal information of Florida residents (reasonable measures, 501.171(2); disposal, 501.171(8)); GBS maintains systems for each subsidiary as its third-party agent (501.171(6)); the intercompany services agreement sets a 10-day notice from GBS to the affected subsidiary

obligation: Florida Digital Bill of Rights
basis: A controller must exceed $1 billion in global gross annual revenue and also earn 50% or more of revenue from online advertising, operate a consumer smart speaker and voice command service, or operate an app store with at least 250,000 applications. FY2025 revenue (about $4.8 billion) comes from distribution, home services, manufacturing and consumer lending, and the group runs no smart speaker service or app store

obligation: Recording consent (worked example)
basis: The AI assistant can transcribe meetings; laws differ by state, and the group applies all-party prior consent in all six states, with Florida as the worked example

obligation: Equal Credit Opportunity Act and Regulation B (credit models and adverse action)
basis: Finance makes consumer credit decisions with the credit underwriting model and uses models in fraud review and collections

obligation: Federal employment discrimination law (Title VII; ADEA) applied to selection tools
basis: The group's employers hire through GBS HR recruiting; the statutes apply to hiring decisions whatever tool is used

obligation: Regulation FD and the insider trading policy
basis: SEC registrant; MNPI in deal rooms and earnings drafts

obligation: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
citation: PCI DSS (card network rules, through merchant agreements)
basis: Building Products and Home Services accept cards; PCI duties are contractual and assessed each year by a separate PCI program

obligation: Sanctions screening before any ransom payment
basis: Applies to all U.S. persons; the cyber policy also requires insurer approval before any ransom payment

obligation: Federal contract clauses on covered telecommunications and Kaspersky products
basis: No federal prime contracts or subcontracts in the contract repository; recheck if one is signed

obligation: State consumer lender licensing duties (Finance)
citation: Consumer lender licensing laws of the six license states
basis: Finance holds consumer lender licenses in all six states; incident notice duties under each license are checked with counsel

obligation: Colorado SB26-189 (AI decision rules for deployers)
basis: Applies to deployers doing business in Colorado; the group and Finance operate only in six southeastern states. Recheck before any expansion

obligation: SL-1 dealer agreements and SL-2 customer agreements (availability, notice and assurance terms)
basis: SL-1 commits to 99.9% monthly availability and 72-hour dealer notice and provides an annual SOC 2 Type 2 report; SL-2 commits to 99.5% availability and 72-hour notice, and two customers require a SOC 2 Type 2 report at their 2027 renewals

obligation: Treasury services agreements, credit facility and securitization documents, and the cyber insurance policy (notice terms)
citation: Bank, lender, trustee and insurer contracts
basis: Bank fraud notice and recall, lender and trustee notices, and insurer notice are contractual duties

obligation: NIST CSF 2.0 group profile (Govern emphasis)
basis: The vertical's benchmark for holding companies; the 10-K Item 1C describes a CSF 2.0-aligned program, and the group keeps current and target profiles
